newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.

text.p: The sorghum market continued to be quiet this week, with most consumers appearing either covered through until at least the end of September or comfortable to stand-aside from the market for the time being, Grainco's Trading Manager Rob Brealey said in his weekly market report.
Brealey said growers also are reluctant to commit any further tonnage at this stage, watching the July weather for longer-term price direction.

Grainco said prices have remained relatively steady over the past week, with some trade at levels around A$128-130/mt on farm for July pick-up, while in central Queensland there has been some selling interest at levels around A$95-A$105/mt on farm (depending on location).
There still appears to be considerable sorghum stock remaining unsold in both southern and central Queensland, together with significant holdings of farmer stocks on the Liverpool Plains.

While the large amount of unsold stock is largely responsible for maintaining a cap on domestic prices at the moment, continuing dry conditions along the east coast are likely to support values longer-term, he said.

Continued concerns regarding the affect on production of the El Nino weather pattern has given some support to barley export prices in January/February 1998 with feed barley from Australia for this deferred position equivalent to US$130 fob Australian port.
Lack of further planting rain in Queensland has given domestic support to new crop prices.

Domestic old crop feed barley prices ended the week higher at around A$177.50/mt delivered Brisbane for July, reflecting a significant premium over export prices which have moved lower at around US$120/mt on an fob basis.
New crop prices finished the week higher at A$155/mt delivered Brisbane for November-December and A$160/mt for strict October delivery.
New crop malting barley prices continue to be su ported in the international market and ended the week at A$185/mt delivered Brisbane port.

Dry conditons across the eastern states has prompted an increase in domestic cottonseed feed demand. This surge is being compounded with the run down to the completion of ginning as consumers endeavour to get hold of stock prior to carry charges kicking in.

Brealey said seed availability is slowly becoming tighter, and although stocks held in Queensland and northern New South Wales (NSW) are considerable, prices are likely to creep up steadily in response.

Cash prices over the past week have firmed slightly with Downs gins trading at A$157/mt to the grower. In central Queensland the July price continues to be quoted at A$150/mt, August at A$155/mt with a carry there after.

"Some interest was beginning to be expressed in pulse pricing from growers during the week. Although at best only tentative at present, spurred by the concern of a few market analysts that prices may falter as the season progresses, pricing of a portion of anticipated production should be considered," he said.

Chickpea and faba bean markets are soft at present due to adequate coverage in consuming markets. However, in the case of chickpeas, once recently shipped product is distributed in the Indian market and the full extent of their monsoon is realised, prices may well recover. The extent of which will become apparent over time.

In contrast the faba bean market may continue to struggle this coming season. Consuming countries look to be well covered for the immediate future and a carry-out of old crop product in the southern states is likely to limit gains. This may turn around with increased demand in the case of a poorer than
expected Egyptian harvest.
Price indications for the new crop chickpeas remain at A$320/mt. Indicative prices for faba beans remain at around A$240/mt to A$250/mt.
Oilseed prices were down with sunflowers finishing the week at A$307/mt delivered Brisbane for July-August and A$317/mt delivered Newcastle for July-August delivery.

Central Queensland sunflower prices were down to A$262-267/mt delivered central Queensland (depending on location) for the July-August delivery period. New crop soybean prices remained steady at A$365/mt delivered Brisbane for
March/May 1998, while new crop sunflowers finished the week at A$330/mt delivered Brisbane for January/April 1998.
